chunks: 69 - Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far عليه السلام said:

“For ghusl (ritual bath), a sāʿ of water, and for wudu (ablution), a mudd of water. The sāʿ of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله is five amdād, and the mudd is the weight of two hundred and eighty dirhams. The dirham is six dānīqs, and the dānīq is the weight of six grains, and the grain is the weight of two grains of barley from the middle-sized grain, not from its small ones nor from its large ones.”

key_terms.أَمْدَادٍ: plural of mudd, used to define the prophetic sāʿ
key_terms.الْغُسْلِ: ghusl, the ritual bath requiring a prescribed measure of water
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu, ritual ablution performed with a smaller measured amount of water
key_terms.دَوَانِيقَ: dānīqs, smaller subdivisions of the dirham
key_terms.دِرْهَمًا: a dirham, a weight unit used to quantify the mudd
key_terms.شَعِيرٍ: barley, used as the reference grain for determining weight
key_terms.صَاعٌ: a sāʿ, a standard volume measure used here for ghusl
key_terms.مُدٌّ: a mudd, a smaller standard measure used here for wudu

ai.seo_question: How much water is required for ghusl and wudu according to Imam Musa ibn Ja'far عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states the measured amount of water for ghusl and wudu, giving precise traditional units for each. It also explains the weight relationships between the sāʿ, mudd, dirham, dānīq, and barley grains, establishing a legal standard for ritual purity according to the prophetic measure.
